text:
maya: Heads up — after last night's kernel-selector change we're seeing a ~10% p95 latency regression on Llama-3 (13B) chat workloads. Metric spike around 03:40 UTC. Suspect KV cache churn + fallback kernels. profiler dump below.

liam: can you paste the selector logs and a perf profile? which model variant (rmsnorm/SiLU)?

maya: model variant: llm-3-13b-rmsnorm. Selector logs: 
```
[2026-03-18T03:39:12Z] kernel-selector: chosen=matmul-opt-v1 fallback=matmul-generic reason=head_dim_mismatch
[2026-03-18T03:39:12Z] kv-cache: evict=3/10 active_sets=2 backlog=0.85
[2026-03-18T03:39:12Z] batcher: avg_batch=6 median=4 p95=12 tail_mode=enabled
```
Profiler snapshot (top ops): 
```
op: matmul (matmul-generic)    time=42.3ms   tokens=128
op: rms_norm                  time=6.1ms
op: kv-cache-lookup           time=18.7ms   hits=0.62
op: attention (kv-merge)      time=24.9ms
```
Note the selector switched to generic matmul for many calls.

perf-bot: [alert] regression: p95 latency +9.8% for llm-3-13b-rmsnorm. Ticket RED-3121 created.

sam: hmm — the "head_dim_mismatch" reason stands out. We recently tightened kernel constraints so some 32->64 head dim combos drop to generic kernels. Did model come in with non-standard head_dim or weird hidden_size/heads pairing?

marta: I checked the model metadata: hidden_size=8192, num_heads=64, head_dim=128 -> that's standard. But config had rope_theta set to 10000 (we defaulted to 5120 in the selector heuristics). If rope scaling influences stride assumptions, selector might reject optimized kernels. Also noticed a new quantization knob in the canary that triggers fallback when seq_len > 512. Chat traffic had longer context (700-900 tokens) around the spike.

diego: two orthogonal things to try: 1) relax the strict head_dim check so it allows matmul-opt-v1 when head_dim is multiple-of-64 (fast path). 2) increase kv-cache eviction threshold so we don't thrash the cache under long contexts. Current kv.max_backlog=0.8; try 0.95 for canary.

sam: for immediate canary, force kernel selection to matmul-opt-v1 + bump kv.max_backlog. command to run in canary policy: 
```
redwoodctl rollout canary set --selector-override "matmul-opt-v1" --selector-scope "llm-3-13b-rmsnorm" --kv-max-backlog 0.95
```
I'll also open a small PR to loosen the head_dim guard in kernel-selector.

marta: opened PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1223 with tests and a micro-benchmark. Also added a tuning profile to prefer v1 for seq_len>512 where latency benefit persists.

liam: curious — did we see any increase in token compute cost (CPU/GPU) when fallback happened? profiler shows matmul-generic is ~3.2x slower per-matmul than matmul-opt-v1 for these dims. That matches the p95 hit.

maya: running the canary now with the override. Will watch p95 and kv hit-rate. If p95 drops back we can promote and then follow up with selector heuristics.

diego: also let's add a lightweight tracer around kv eviction to correlate client-level context lengths to eviction events. Short-term: add logs, long-term: adapt eviction policy by observed context distribution.

marta: noted — added tracer TODO to PR and a dashboard widget (per-route kv_hit_rate vs context_len).

maya: initial canary results: p95 down from +9.8% to +1.1% after forcing matmul-opt-v1 and kv.max_backlog bump. kv_hit_rate improved from 62% -> 81%.

sam: great. Next steps: merge PR 1223, revert the strict constraint in selector, ship a rolling canary to 10% with the new defaults, and schedule a follow-up to tune rope_theta heuristics. I'll file RED-3122 for the rope/defaults audit.

maya: thanks everyone :thumbsup: closing thread, will update RED-3121 with metrics and promote if stable.
